articles.title: Serena Williams bought a 2.7-acre Bel-Air estate with a 6,101-sq-ft mansion; after repeated price cuts, it sold for $8.1 million after being listed for nearly $12 million
articles.summary: International Sports News: Serena Williams sold her long-held Bel-Air estate for $8.1 million in April 2019, ending a sale process that lasted about 18 months. The tennis star h.
articles.body: Serena Williams sold her long-held Bel-Air estate for $8.1 million in April 2019, ending a sale process that lasted about 18 months. The tennis star had bought the property in 2006 for $6.612 million and first listed it in late 2017 for $11.995 million, or nearly $12 million. The 1935-built home sits on about 2.7 acres and has 6,101 square feet of living space, six bedrooms and seven bathrooms. Williams later reduced the asking price to $9.995 million, but the property eventually changed hands for $8.1 million, giving her a gross gain over what she originally paid.What did Serena Williams pay for her Bel-Air estate in 2006Serena Williams bought the Bel-Air property in 2006 for $6.612 million, according to property records reported by The Washington Post. At the time, the home gave her a large private space in one of Los Angeles’ most well-known luxury neighborhoods.The house was built in 1935, so it was not a newly constructed celebrity mansion when Williams bought it. Instead, the property had an older California feel, with plenty of land around the main house. Its location in the Stone Canyon area also gave the estate a level of privacy that is difficult to find on a large residential property in Los Angeles.Williams kept the home for more than a decade. During those years, her life changed in major ways, both on and off the tennis court, while the Bel-Air house remained one of her main Los Angeles properties.Why did Serena Williams list the Bel-Air mansion for nearly $12 millionWilliams put the property on the market in late 2017 with an asking price of $11.995 million. The timing came after she welcomed her daughter, Olympia, in September 2017, and married Alexis Ohanian.Around the same period, Williams and Ohanian bought a newer home in the Beverly Hills area for about $6.7 million. That five-bedroom property was built with features aimed at modern family living, including a pool, wine cellar and yoga room.The move meant Williams no longer needed to keep the older Bel-Air estate as her main Los Angeles home. The Bel-Air house was much larger in terms of land, but the newer property offered a different kind of setup for the family.The initial $11.995 million price was also well above what Williams had paid for the house. At that figure, the estate was being offered for roughly $5.4 million more than its 2006 purchase price.What was inside Serena Williams’ 6,101-square-foot Bel-Air mansionThe Bel-Air home had six bedrooms, seven bathrooms and about 6,101 square feet of living space. It was built across a large, tree-filled property, giving the house a more private setting than its street address might suggest.Inside, the home had marble and hardwood floors, high ceilings and a large living room. The living room included a curved wall of clerestory windows and French doors that opened toward the greenery outside. There was also a dark wood executive office or study and a wet bar.The main bedroom area was larger than a standard bedroom suite. It included a sitting area, dressing rooms and a large bathroom.One of the home’s more unusual features was a full-service hair salon. That stood out even among the property’s other luxury features and suited Williams’ busy life in tennis, fashion and public appearances.The estate also had a gym and a three-car garage. Outside, the grounds included a swimming pool, pool house, gardens, covered patio areas and private walking trails.Despite being owned by one of tennis’ greatest players, the property did not have a tennis court.How much did Serena Williams reduce the Bel-Air asking priceThe original $11.995 million asking price did not bring a sale quickly. After the property had spent months on the market, Williams cut the price by about $2 million in April 2018.The new asking price was $9.995 million. That was still nearly $3.4 million above the $6.612 million Williams had paid for the home in 2006, but it was a major step down from the original listing.The house continued to sit on the market. By the time it sold, the final price was much lower than both of the earlier asking prices.The Los Angeles Times reported that the property finally sold for $8.1 million in April 2019. That meant Williams accepted about $3.895 million less than the original $11.995 million asking price.How much profit did Serena Williams make from the $8.1 million saleOn the basic purchase price alone, Williams still made money from the sale. She paid $6.612 million for the property in 2006 and sold it for $8.1 million in 2019.That puts the difference at about $1.488 million before expenses linked to the sale, such as commissions, taxes and other closing costs. So the $8.1 million transaction was not a loss compared with her original purchase price.At the same time, the final sale was far below the number Serena Williams had hoped to get when she first listed the home. The gap between the initial asking price and the final sale price was close to $3.9 million.For a property that stayed with Williams for about 13 years, the final deal therefore tells two different parts of the story: she did not get close to the original $12 million target, but she also sold the estate for more than she had paid for it.The Bel-Air sale closed a long chapter in Williams’ Los Angeles real estate history. The 2.7-acre property had been part of her life since 2006, but after her family grew and her housing plans changed, the older estate was eventually sold for $8.1 million.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: Barry Melrose, longtime NHL player, coach and ESPN icon, dies at 70 after battle with Parkinson's
articles.summary: Barry Melrose stepped away from ESPN in 2023 after revealing his Parkinson's diagnosis.
articles.body:
Former NHL player, coach and iconic ESPN hockey analyst Barry Melrose died on Wednesday, his wife Cindy confirmed to ESPN.

Melrose was diagnosed with Parkinson's disease in 2023. He stepped away from his role at ESPN at the time as a result of his diagnosis, ending a nearly three-decade run at the network where he had become a fixture in the sport while constantly working the biggest events throughout the NHL each season. Melrose was perhaps the most recognizable hockey broadcaster in the nation, thanks in part to his trademark slicked-back hair and goatee.

"For decades, Barry Melrose was one of the most distinctive and trusted voices in hockey," ESPN said in a statement . "His knowledge of the game was deep, his candor was refreshing and his passion was unmistakable. He was a foundational part of ESPN's hockey coverage, and fans and teammates truly appreciated his entertaining delivery and charismatic personality. "We send our deepest condolences to his loved ones. He always kept it interesting and he will be missed."

"We send our deepest condolences to his loved ones. He always kept it interesting and he will be missed."

Melrose spent seven seasons as a defenseman in the NHL with the Winnipeg Jets , Toronto Maple Leafs and Detroit Red Wings , which came after a three-year run with the Cincinnati Stingers in the WHA. He had 10 goals, 33 points and an incredible 728 penalty minutes in his 300 NHL games throughout his career.

Melrose transitioned into coaching after his playing career ended. He spent three seasons leading the Los Angeles Kings , most notably with Wayne Gretzky during their run to the Stanley Cup Final in 1993. He briefly came out of retirement in 2009 for a 16-game stint to coach the Tampa Bay Lightning . In total, he held an 84-108-29 record as a coach in the league.

Plenty of Melrose's ESPN colleagues took to social media to remember him on Wednesday night.

NHL commissioner Gary Bettman released a statement paying tribute to Melrose.

"From the flowing locks of his distinctive mullet to the flared lapels of his trademark long suit coats, Barry Melrose cut an unmistakable figure whenever you were fortunate enough to run into him at a rink or catch him on your television screen," Bettman said . "You were even more fortunate if you engaged him in conversation or listened to his analysis, because he never failed to boost your love of the game of hockey. "A rangy and rugged defenseman from Kelvington, Saskatchewan, Barry fashioned an 11-year pro career in the NHL, AHL and WHA. But it was as a coach, who guided the Los Angeles Kings to the 1993 Stanley Cup Final, and as a broadcaster, who spent 27 years at ESPN, that he truly made his mark upon the game. And during those countless encounters over the years with players, coaches, fans and viewers who couldn't help but be drawn in by his enthusiasm. "We mourn the passing of a hockey original. The defenseman appeared in 300 career NHL games.

After that, he coached the Seattle Thunderbirds before he led the Adirondack Red Wings of the American Hockey League to the Calder Cup title in 1991.

He then coached Wayne Gretzky and the Los Angeles Kings for three seasons from 1992-95 and led them to the Stanley Cup Final in his first season.

Following that coaching stint, he joined ESPN in 1996 and remained with the network until he coached the Tampa Bay Lightning for 16 games during the 2008-09 season.

Many younger fans who did not see him play or coach got to know Melrose as a broadcaster for ESPN.

articles.title: Chess by day, Salem by night: Board games, tennis and Nihal Sarin's 7 am GCL night
articles.summary: Chess News: BENGALURU: The ITC Windsor hotel, home to the six teams competing in the 2026 Global Chess League (GCL), sits at the heart of the city. Walk in after .
articles.body: BENGALURU: The ITC Windsor hotel, home to the six teams competing in the 2026 Global Chess League (GCL), sits at the heart of the city. Walk in after the security check at the gate, past doormen greeting you with folded hands, and a left turn down the hallway from reception leads to the dining area, where Dutch No. 1 Anish Giri can be found sipping a hot chocolate latte beside his Alpine Pipers teammate and close friend Vidit Gujrathi. Look towards the other corner and Levon Aronian and Maxime Vachier-Lagrave are reading the morning newspaper.For Nihal Sarin, the most effective player for the American Gambits so far this season, the time on the clock matters little here. For him, it is still midnight. And why wouldn't it be? "We stayed up till around 7 am," Nihal told TimesofIndia.com in an exclusive interaction on Wednesday. "We were playing a board game called Salem. It's a social deduction game."Among those who stayed up late with him was his American Gambits teammate and World Championship challenger Javokhir Sindarov, an avowed video game enthusiast who, by his own admission, played Counter-Strike between rounds during his Candidates win in Cyprus earlier this year. "Sindarov is a good friend of mine, very humble, and down to earth. He is very chill and always smiling," the 22-year-old added.Video games, however, have never held the same pull for Nihal. Suggest a game of padel or a board game instead, and he'll be the first to put his hand up.Tuesday's late night, though, wasn't about squeezing in one more round of board games. It was about waiting up for the US Open men's quarterfinal between Ben Shelton and Carlos Alcaraz.But even staying awake till 7 am wasn't quite enough; the match was delayed after the preceding women's quarterfinal between Jessica Pegula and Emma Navarro ran long, and Nihal, a long-time tennis fan, eventually lost his battle with sleep.Amid a schedule that has him playing almost two games of intense rapid chess almost every day, Nihal hasn't lost track of the sport he has followed for years. And what about the Williams sisters' return to professional tennis? "I didn't expect that at all," he said while raising both his eyebrows. "The tendency to even compete at that level at that age is truly extraordinary."For Nihal, anyone who has been at the top of their game and is still putting in the work to prove it deserves to be called an "absolute legend."In the context of the GCL, that applies just as much to five-time World Champion Viswanathan Anand, who has had a quiet season for his new team, Alaskan Knights. The 56-year-old has been winless in six games, with only two draws. But the poor form hasn't dented his legacy as a chess icon even a bit in Nihal's eyes."People are there to take shots at him, but Vishy doesn't give a crap about their opinion. And that is why he is a legend," Nihal said. "The FIDE role and everything don't matter much here, but the way he has performed in some of these games here is simply outstanding at this age."Chess Olympiad in focus Nihal is part of the Indian team preparing to defend its Open title at the Chess Olympiad in Samarkand, Uzbekistan, later this month, which will also be his first appearance in India's main Olympiad squad.He is, by his own description, excited and thrilled about it."I am very happy because we are all friends and have been together from the start, except for Vidit," he quipped. "He is the old one, not from our generation. But jokes aside, Vidit is a top player who has already won gold for India at that level (Olympiad)."Grandmaster and coach Srinath Narayanan led an intense pre-Olympiad training camp for the Indian team in late August to prepare for Samarkand. Nihal was a part of it.While the Kerala-born Grandmaster did not reveal many details about the camp, he acknowledged, “Virtual camps are not as helpful as in-person ones. But I am very much excited for the Olympiad,” before signing off casually, “I will go and take a nap after my breakfast.” It was already 2:30 pm on the clock.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: Barry Melrose cause of death: How did the former player, coach and ESPN analyst die at 70
articles.summary: NHL News: Barry Melrose, one of the most recognizable faces in hockey broadcasting, died Wednesday at the age of 70. His wife, Cindy, confirmed the passing to E.
articles.body: Barry Melrose, one of the most recognizable faces in hockey broadcasting, died Wednesday at the age of 70. His wife, Cindy, confirmed the passing to ESPN, which broke the news to a hockey world that had not forgotten the man who spent decades shaping how fans understood the sport. Melrose had been diagnosed with Parkinson's disease in 2023, leading to his retirement from ESPN after nearly 30 years with the network. His death drew immediate tributes from across the NHL, the broadcasting world, and beyond.What was Barry Melrose's cause of death?Barry Melrose died following a battle with Parkinson's disease. The illness had already forced him out of public life two years earlier. When he announced his retirement in October 2023, he said: "I've had over 50 extraordinary years playing, coaching and analyzing the world's greatest game, hockey. It's now time to hang up my skates and focus on my health, my family, including my supportive wife Cindy, and whatever comes next."ESPN did not formally confirm Parkinson's disease as the official cause of death, but the timeline is clear. The diagnosis came just as the 2023-24 NHL season opened, and he never returned to the desk. When ESPN's Steve Levy announced on the eve of the 2023 Stanley Cup Final that Melrose would not continue their long streak of covering the series together, it led many in the hockey community to suspect something was wrong. That suspicion turned out to be correct.Melrose was 67 when he got the diagnosis. He was gone at 70.How did Barry Melrose build his legacy across playing, coaching and broadcasting?Melrose finished his NHL playing career with 10 goals, 33 points, and 728 penalty minutes across 300 regular season games. He suited up for the Winnipeg Jets, Toronto Maple Leafs, and Detroit Red Wings. The stats tell you what kind of player he was: hard-nosed, physical, not there to fill up the scoresheet. What he was building, though, was something harder to quantify.As a coach, he took the Wayne Gretzky-led Kings to the precipice of their first Stanley Cup in 1993 in his first season guiding an NHL team. That run was stunning. Los Angeles lost to the Montreal Canadiens in five games, but the Kings had never been there before, and Melrose had gotten them there in year one. He continued coaching the Kings for two more seasons, finishing both years out of the playoffs with losing records. Just 30 minutes after the Kings fired him in April 1995, Melrose was signed by ESPN to work as a studio analyst during the upcoming NHL playoffs. That timing says a lot about how the network saw him.His television career defined him to a new generation of fans. Known for his sense of humor, his mullet, and his fancy suits, Melrose became a star on ESPN, endearing himself to hockey fans everywhere. He had a way of making the game feel approachable without ever dumbing it down. When asked what he wanted viewers to take away from watching him, he told the Los Angeles Times in 1995: "When [people] watch me on TV, I want them to go, 'Geez, I'd like to go for a beer with Barry Melrose and talk hockey. He seems like he'd be very interesting.'"NHL Commissioner Gary Bettman paid tribute after the news broke.ESPN's John Buccigross wrote: "Barry was my best friend at ESPN. A big brother figure of rock solid values. I am shook to my core. Barry gave his life to hockey and some of his ESPN family, like me, learned of his shocking death today while at a hockey rink in Las Vegas preparing for the upcoming season. Chilling and fitting — the rink was Barry's home. A more beloved ESPN institution there has not been. We love you, Barry. Forever."Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

articles.title: ‘The arrow will for sure be a 10’: Jyothi Surekha Vennam’s simple mantra ahead of Asian Games
articles.summary: More sports News: New Delhi: For Jyothi Surekha Vennam, the mantra ahead of the Asian Games is deceptively simple: perfect the process and let the scoreboard take care .
articles.body: New Delhi: For Jyothi Surekha Vennam, the mantra ahead of the Asian Games is deceptively simple: perfect the process and let the scoreboard take care of itself. India’s No. 1 women’s compound archer and a major medal hope, Jyothi will arrive in Aichi-Nagoya for her remarkable fourth Asian Games appearance. At Hangzhou in 2023, she produced a golden sweep, winning gold in the individual, women’s team and mixed team events. She has won medals at every edition of the multisport event.The 30-year-old told TOI that her emphasis was on executing each shot cleanly rather than dwelling on expectations. “Right now, I am just focused on myself and on shooting my best. This is the mindset I am going with,” she said, adding, “I’m not chasing results or scores. I know that if I execute my shot really well, the arrow will for sure be a 10.”Jyothi will spearhead a new-look trio featuring Chikitha Taniparthi and Prithika Pradeep, with the team having competed together at World Cups. She is also set to compete in the individual, women’s team and mixed team events, placing her at the heart of India’s campaign. “We are working together as a team to give great performances at the Games. I’m confident about the way things are going right now,” she said,The preparation has been meticulous. At SAI Sonipat, phase two of the national camp has involved archery-specific physical work, two daily practice sessions plus psychology, physiotherapy and gym work. The squad leaves for Japan on Friday and will spend about 10 days training in Kurobe City before entering the Games village.There is no dramatic technical overhaul. “I haven’t made any changes to my equipment or myself,” said Jyothi, who is supported by and training at the Inspire Institute of Sport (IIS). Her biggest sharpening has been mental: “Reading, visualisation and brief meditation keep me calm and focused.” Her approach is equally practical when sessions falter: analyse execution, check equipment, accept bad days and move forward without surrendering confidence or composure.South Korea remains a formidable rival but Jyothi warns against overlooking other Asian teams, saying surprises can emerge from a field where everyone understands the stakes. “The South Koreans are tough competitiors but you can’t underestimate any other Asian country. Everyone is doing a really great job, working hard.”The stakes are higher than medals as the Asian Games offer Olympic qualification opportunities, including a quota linked to the mixed team compound event, adding significance ahead of the Los Angeles Games.Jyothi also spoke about the disappointment of another Khel Ratna snub and said it’s natural for an athlete to “feel bad”. “But I can’t let things that are personal affect the team as a whole,” she said.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: Injury forces Commonwealth Games silver medallist Rishikanta out of Asian Games
articles.summary: More sports News: Kolkata: Manipur’s Rishikanta Singh Chanambam, who won a silver medal in the men’s 60kg weightlifting competition at the Commonwealth Games in Glasgow.
articles.body: Kolkata: Manipur’s Rishikanta Singh Chanambam, who won a silver medal in the men’s 60kg weightlifting competition at the Commonwealth Games in Glasgow, has been forced to pull out of India’s Asian Games squad because of an injury.Speaking to TOI on Wednesday from Manipur, Rishikanta said, “I had been dealing with pain on the left side of my knee even during the Commonwealth Games. I really wanted to compete in the Asiad too because it’s a big competition for me, but I couldn’t manage it. I later consulted a doctor, who said there was a muscle imbalance on my left side. Right now, I’m focusing on my recovery.”Rishikanta was the lone male athlete in India’s weightlifting squad for the continental meet, which will be held in Aichi Prefecture and Nagoya, Japan, from Sept 19 to Oct 4.Besides Rishikanta, the four other athletes who’s been named in the squad were Mirabai Chanu (women’s 49kg), Gyaneshwari Yadav (women’s 53kg), Seram Nirupama Devi (women’s 61kg) and Harjinder Kaur (women’s 69kg).At the last Asian Games, India had sent a two-member weightlifting team comprising Mirabai and Bindyarani Devi, but neither finished on the podium. Mirabai finished fourth in the 49kg category, while Bindyarani was fifth in the 55kg category.Rishikanta will be gutted to miss the Games after his success in Glasgow. Following his performance there, he had said that, had it not been for the injury, he would have gone for gold.Malaysia’s Bin Kasdan Mohamad Aniq eventually won the event with a Games-record total of 273kg. Rishikanta lifted a total of 264kg. He equalled Bin Kasdan’s 121kg in the snatch but could manage only 143kg in the clean and jerk, compared to the Malaysian’s 152kg.For now, the 21-year-old is keeping his focus on recovery, hoping to return stronger and make up for the opportunity he has missed.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: ‘No parent is comfortable’: K Humpy pinpoints hurdle holding girls back in chess
articles.summary: Chess News: Bengaluru: K Humpy, India’s first-ever woman chess player to attain a Grandmaster title, has witnessed dramatic changes to the landscape of the cerebr.
articles.body: Bengaluru: K Humpy, India’s first-ever woman chess player to attain a Grandmaster title, has witnessed dramatic changes to the landscape of the cerebral sport over the last 30-odd years.“Chess was not a commercial sport and women’s chess was not at all (commercial). So even after I became a GM, after being women’s world No. 2 for many years, there was not much money involved in the sport. When I won the Grand Prix, I think my prize money was about 6,000 euros,” said 39-year-old Humpy after her team Alpine APL Pipers, led by Magnus Carlsen on the top board, defeated Mumba Masters 11-6 in the Global Chess League (GCL) on Wednesday.“Now, you have Cairns Cup and Norway Chess, where the first prize for women is about 60,000 euros. The Tata Steel Rapid & Blitz event in India also gives equal prize to women, plus starting fees (appearance money). Sport is becoming more commercial. So, if you have the talent, you can sustain professionally.”Still, very few U-15 girls the world over belong to the Elo 2000 rating bracket, only about 60 compared to 850 boys.Asked what is stopping the vast majority of girls who shine at the age-group girls’ events but remain far off from the GM title, Humpy said: “The major difference is that the parents give more freedom to boys to go to any chess club or to someone’s house. So, they’ll sit with other boys and male players and start working. But when it comes to teenage girls, no parent is comfortable sending a girl alone.“If we have regular training camps where the girls will come and attend along with other boys and with some International Masters or GMs, they’ll definitely pick up fast. I don’t know who can do it, state body, (national) federation or maybe some private parties,” Humpy said.Results (Day 5): APL Pipers 11 bt Mumba Masters 6, Triveni Kings 3 lost to Ganges Grandmasters 15, Mumba 6 lost to Alaskan Knights 11, American Gambits 8 bt Triveni 5.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.summary: Chess News: BENGALURU: It was a different day, a different set of fixtures and a different proposition for each team looking to seal a top-two berth. But what rem.
articles.body: BENGALURU: It was a different day, a different set of fixtures and a different proposition for each team looking to seal a top-two berth. But what remained the same was Viswanathan Anand’s miserable run at the 2026 Global Chess League (GCL) on Wednesday at The Lalit Ashok Hotel. This time, the defeat came against veteran Grandmaster Maxime Vachier-Lagrave, who had White pieces.Although Anand’s side, Alaskan Knights, ended up winning the match against MVL’s Mumba Masters, the Indian legend, still winless with five defeats from seven games, has endured a complicated outing despite producing competitive performances and showing glimpses of brilliance on the "Icon" board against some of the strongest players in the field.After the match, fellow Indian Grandmaster and Anand's teammate Arjun Erigaisi spoke to the media about the veteran's difficult run and why his results do not tell the whole story.Asked about Anand’s recent lack of form on the board, Arjun replied, “At this age, I cannot imagine how many people would be playing at this level. Even though he lost some games, it wasn't like he was getting outplayed or something.”Arjun stressed that Anand, now 56, continues to compete on equal terms with a younger generation of players.“He is still competing head-on with most of these young players. Only in the final moments, some unfortunate things are happening,” he added. “It's hugely inspiring to see how well he is playing at this age.”The 23-year-old also discussed the conversations players have away from the board, particularly after wins and losses, and how they deal with mistakes.“Just analyse the important things that happened and try to rectify whatever can be done,” he revealed. “For example, I was missing a lot of basic tactics in earlier games. articles.title: Dodgers announce decision on Shohei Ohtani injury
articles.summary: Los Angeles Dodgers superstar Shohei Ohtani has missed six of the past seven games with discomfort in his right arm. As a result, the Dodgers have decided to...
articles.body:
Los Angeles Dodgers superstar Shohei Ohtani has missed six of the past seven games with discomfort in his right arm. As a result, the Dodgers have decided to put him on the injured list.

Following the team's 14-1 win over the Cincinnati Reds on Wednesday night, Dodgers manager Dave Roberts told reporters that Ohtani would be headed to the injured list and the team would be calling up top outfield prospect Josue De Paula from Double-A to temporarily take his place at designated hitter.

Ohtani has not pitched since July 3 as a result of soreness in his left knee, which returned when he tried to throw his most recent bullpen session on Aug. 28. On Monday, Ohtani acknowledged that he will "most likely" not pitch again this season. However, he hasn't exactly been healthy on the offensive side of the game, either.

The injury concerns began last Wednesday, when Ohtani shook his right arm as he walked into the dugout after a 10th-inning strikeout. After the injury, Ohtani was not in the lineup the following day, and he then missed games on Friday, Saturday, and Sunday too.

Ohtani returned to the lineup on Monday, where he went 0-for-3 with a walk and two strikeouts, but he was out of the lineup again on Tuesday. Roberts said Ohtani complained of pain in his right arm during one of his swings on Monday, prompting the team to think more seriously about placing him on the IL.

After Wednesday's game, Roberts officially announced the move.

Roberts told reporters that putting Ohtani on the IL was "the right thing to do," adding, "We tried to kick the can as much as we could."

That said, Roberts said that he was "very" confident that Ohtani would be ready to return to the team by the time the postseason begins.

"If it were a postseason game tomorrow, he would be in the lineup," Roberts said via ESPN . "Now you're talking about two weeks, 14 days. I feel that it's that substantial. He'll be in a much better place than he was today. Is it gonna be 100%? Probably not. But I do think, with this time that we're taking now, he'll be in an adequate spot to finish the season and beyond."

The soonest that Ohtani will be eligible to return from the 15-day IL is Sept. 23.

articles.title: Why Yankees' Cam Schlittler is going to win AL Cy Young over Dylan Cease
articles.summary: His latest start may have been overshadowed by the much-anticipated return of three-time American League MVP Aaron Judge. Still, New York Yankees starting pi...
articles.body:
His latest start may have been overshadowed by the much-anticipated return of three-time American League MVP Aaron Judge. Still, New York Yankees starting pitcher Cam Schlittler once again padded his case to be the 2026 American League Cy Young Award winner as he dealt seven innings of one-run baseball and struck out 10 batters in a 5-3 win over the Colorado Rockies Tuesday night.

Despite the season that Toronto Blue Jays ace Dylan Cease has put together, it is evident that the 25-year-old has separated himself from the pack. As the Yankees attempt to end the season on a high note and enter the 2026 postseason playing their best baseball, Schlittler will have a chance to achieve a special personal milestone, even if his mind won't be pushed towards thinking about such a self-serving narrative with less than a month remaining in the regular season.

"Pushing that to the side and focusing on these last three weeks. I feel like it's been good so far but a lot of things can happen," Schlittler told reporters after the win. "If I go out there and do my job and put this team in position to win, that opportunity might be there."

Cam Schlittler is atop the sport in several important statistics

Schlittler has gone 13-6 with a 2.01 ERA, a 2.60 FIP, and 220 strikeouts across 178.2 innings thus far . He leads the AL in ERA. Further, he ranks second in innings pitched, third in strikeouts, and second in WHIP.

According to Baseball Savant, he ranks in the 99th percentile in terms of Pitching Run Value, the 100th percentile in Fastball Run Value, and the 95th percentile in K%.

"I feel like I've been able to gradually build up those innings each season in the Minor Leagues," Schlitter told Bryan Hoch of MLB.com. "I feel like, yeah, I'm in a really good spot. I feel like I've been able to take care of my stuff and rely on my teammates and the staff to really push me through that."

Voters could view Schlittler's season as more impactful given his age

With his latest outing, the Massachusetts native extended his franchise record with 20 starts this season of giving up one run or fewer. Additionally, many of the phenom's aforementioned statistics will be considered career highs or career bests by the end of his regular season.

Writers may view Schlittler's season as more impactful and impressive given his age. Of course, one could just as easily say that the 30-year-old Cease is just as noteworthy since he's been able to be dominant in his eighth season, but New York's trusty righty has also outdone the Milton native in several areas to this point.

Cease has been a solid pitcher since his breakout season with the Chicago White Sox in 2021, but Schlittler's sophomore dominance has been transformative for a New York squad that has prided itself on having a deadly rotation that can shut down any lineup.

Even with arms like Gerrit Cole , Max Fried , and Carlos Rodon , Schlittler has stood out as a starter that opposing teams would rather not face. While the other three talents have each dealt with injuries at different points in 2026, the former seventh-round pick has been a staunch presence in the Yankees' rotation. He's regularly been able to provide quality starts and be a guaranteed

Whether or not the Yankees achieve their ultimate goal of winning the franchise's 28th World Series remains to be seen, but Schlittler's sensational sophomore year should place him in prime position to bring home some prestigious hardware at the end of the season.

"He's been the best pitcher in the league," Yankees manager Aaron Boone said. "When you have that going all year at the top of your rotation, that's massive. And that's what he's been."

articles.title: ‘Going to get a cardiac test’: Seahawks owner Vinod Khosla reacts to wild Patriots comeback
articles.summary: Seattle Seahawks owner Vinod Khosla admitted he may need a cardiac test after watching his team produce a dramatic comeback against the New England Patriots...
articles.body:
Seattle Seahawks owner Vinod Khosla admitted he may need a cardiac test after watching his team produce a dramatic comeback against the New England Patriots in their season opener.

The Seahawks trailed for most of the game before scoring 10 unanswered points in the fourth quarter to complete a 13-10 victory over the Patriots in a rematch of last season's Super Bowl.

Khosla, whose family completed a record-breaking $9.612 billion purchase of the Seahawks last week, was watching on as Seattle recovered from a difficult start to begin the defence of its championship.

Vinod Khosla admits Seahawks win was a "roller coaster"

The Seahawks owner took to X after the final whistle to share his reaction to a game that appeared to be slipping away from Seattle for much of the night.

Khosla wrote: "I'm going to get a cardiac test before the next Seahawks game. The team and 12s won it tonight. Hard to imagine a better roller coaster."

It was certainly a stressful opening game for the new chairman, with Seattle failing to score in the first half and trailing 10-3 heading into the fourth quarter.

Drew Lock had taken over at quarterback after Sam Darnold suffered a hip injury on the opening drive. Lock then found Jaxon Smith-Njigba for a 45-yard touchdown in the fourth quarter before Jason Myers ' field goal completed the comeback.

Smith-Njigba finished with eight receptions for 122 yards and a touchdown, while Lock completed 16 of 22 passes for 187 yards and a score.

The Seahawks defence also played a major role in the turnaround, keeping New England scoreless in the final quarter after Mike Vrabel's side had controlled much of the contest.

Meanwhile, Seattle will be hoping Darnold's injury is not serious after coach Mike Macdonald provided a positive early update following the game.

Macdonald said: "At this point, we're able to rule out a fracture. There are more tests to be done. That's why I'm saying that it's positive [news]. We're still working on that but right now, I think fracture is out, which is great news."

For Khosla, however, the immediate concern was simply getting through a wild first game with a victory. Seattle now has momentum heading into the rest of the season, while the Patriots will have to respond after letting a 10-point advantage slip away.

articles.title: 'I would have loved it' - Anderson on Glasner's wing-back system
articles.summary: Former Nottingham Forest winger Paul Anderson says Oliver Glasner "has the personnel" to play his preferred wing-back system, but believes it will "take time...
articles.body:
Former Nottingham Forest winger Paul Anderson says Oliver Glasner "has the personnel" to play his preferred wing-back system, but believes it will "take time" to fully bear its fruits.

"I've been coaching for over five years now and I love the formation," he told BBC Radio Nottingham's Shut Up And Show More Football podcast.

"It allows you to outnumber an opposition team anywhere on the pitch. It also gives you the option of having two strikers - one of which can drop into the middle of the pitch and give you the option of four midfielders.

"That way, you can either overload the middle of the pitch or go man-to-man when you're playing against a back four.

"You've got to have the personnel to play it, though. You've got to have intelligent players that can drop in and work off each other, and your wing-backs have to be fit.

"It probably would have suited me as a player because I was quite a defensive winger anyway. It would have been hard work, but I would have loved it."

Despite the Reds failing to win any of their opening three league matches this season, Anderson did highlight some positives.

"Nottingham Forest have very strong centre-backs at the minute," he said.

"I've been very impressed by Jair Cunha as well, he has been making it hard for Ousmane Diomande to make it into the team, despite the club spending money on him.

"There is always going to be a question mark over Murillo 's fitness, but if he is fit and at 100% then this formation suits him perfectly. The same goes for Nikola Milenkovic - it is perfect for him.

"It also suits the midfield. It is a formation which is going to allow Morgan Gibbs-White and James McAtee more space in there.

"So they definitely have players in the squad who can do a job in this formation, it is just going to take time to come together."

articles.title: Seahawks HC Mike Macdonald Shares Good News on Sam Darnold Injury
articles.summary: Seattle Seahawks head coach Mike Macdonald revealed that quarterback Sam Darnold did not fracture his hip in the season opener. The post Seahawks HC Mike Mac...
articles.body:
The Seattle Seahawks may have avoided the worst with quarterback Sam Darnold .

After he was hurt in the team's season-opening win over the New England Patriots , head coach Mike Macdonald offered an optimistic outlook. The Seahawks were able to gut out a win with backup Drew Lock at the helm, and now attention turns to Darnold and whether he could miss time beyond the first week.

Sam Darnold Injury News Brings Relief to Seahawks

Immediately after the game, Macdonald addressed fears that Darnold could be out a significant stretch after being hurt early in Wednesday's game.

"Mike Macdonald shares they got 'good news' on Sam Darnold and his hip injury," noted reporter Ethan McReynolds in a post on X.

Macdonald said initial tests showed that Darnold did not suffer a hip fracture on the play.

ESPN's Adam Schefter reported after the game that Darnold had to leave the stadium to undergo testing.

"Sources: Seahawks QB Sam Darnold has been at Harborview Medical Center in Seattle, undergoing a CT scan on his hip," Schefter shared in a post on X. "The initial test was encouraging but inconclusive, and Darnold now is scheduled to undergo an MRI on Thursday."

Darnold was knocked out of the season opener early, going down after the team's first drive. He was diagnosed with a hip injury first listed as questionable before being ruled out of the game later.

As ESPN noted , Darnold suffered the injury when he was sacked by Patriots linebacker Dre'Mont Jones .

Seahawks Could Need Help if Sam Darnold Misses Time

If Darnold were to miss significant time, the Seahawks may need to hit the quarterback market for more depth. They turned to veteran backup Lock in Wednesday's game, watching him lead the Seahawks to 13 unanswered points to win 13-10.

The team has second-year quarterback Jalen Milroe as their emergency quarterback, but it's not clear if the team would trust him as the No. 2 to Lock.

articles.summary: The Houston Texans look like the early winners of their trade with the New England Patriots for wide receiver Kayshon Boutte. The post Patriots Called Out Ov...
articles.body:
The Houston Texans are looking like early winners of their trade for Kayshon Boutte .

Boutte was shipped out by the New England Patriots during training camp, with the Texans sending safety Jaylen Reed and a late-round draft pick in exchange.

Now, following an injury to AJ Brown , the Patriots' decision looks questionable.

"The Patriots moved their other vertical downfield threat with Kayshon Boutte a few weeks ago," Sleeper affiliate Jacob Barzilla posted on X after Brown was forced from New England 's regular-season opener against the Seattle Seahawks with an ankle injury.

"I was already surprised they would move Boutte to a team like Houston and if they miss A.J. Brown for some time…"

The Boston Herald's Andrew Callahan reported seeing Brown leaving in a walking boot.

a snapshot of the Patriots' other receivers.

It included another offseason trade acquisition, Romeo Doubs , for whom the night continued to spiral downward. He had 0 receptions on three targets and a couple of significant drops in his Patriots debut.

"Gunna go out on a limb and say the Patriots are missing Boutte right now," Houston Stressans (Garret Williams) posted .

Patriots quarterback Drake Maye tried to shake off the loss of Brown.

The third-year QB completed 23 of 33 passes for 178 yards, 1 touchdown, and 3 interceptions. Brown finished with three receptions for 26 yards. The injury to Brown puts a spotlight back on their trade, which Patriots brass sold as a win-win.

Patriots Comments About Kayshon Boutte Trade Loom Large

Both Patriots general manager Eliot Wolf and head coach Mike Vrabel downplayed the loss of Boutte to the Texans, a team defeated in the AFC Divisional Round last year.

"There was no concern about that," Wolf told reporters when asked directly about the decision on Boutte in August. "And I don't think there's any concern for them to send us a safety that we think can play."

Vrabel echoed Wolf in that Boutte would have struggled for playing time.

"Without injuries, Kayshon probably would have been inactive, unfortunately," Vrabel told reporters on August 27. "It's kind of the way it was … with him not playing special teams."

Kayshon Boutte Expected to Have Role in Week 1 vs Bills

While the Patriots mull over their decision and await further clarity on Brown, the Texans are expected to implement Boutte into the offense right out of the gate in the Week 1 regular-season opener against the Buffalo Bills .

"Kayshon is learning the playbook very well, and we're throwing it all at him," Texans head coach DeMeco Ryans told media members on September 7.

"The speed of transition is definitely there. He's done a great job of being attentive of what we've asked him to do, and we're throwing him out there. So, let's see. We're trying to go win a football game. We traded for the guy for a reason. Think he's a really good playmaker. So, we want to see that show up on Sunday."

For his part, Boutte said he is ready to make impact plays and help the Texans win.

"I always did believe this team had potential," Boutte told reporters on September 2. "I think, just with this year, we got another chance to get back to that. So, that's the goal."

articles.title: 'Scientific evidence backing my case': Anaya Bangar hits back at critics, claims no 'unfair advantage'
articles.summary: Off the field News: Transgender cricketer Anaya Bangar has responded to criticism over her participation in women’s cricket in Australia, saying she has scientific eviden.
articles.body: Transgender cricketer Anaya Bangar has responded to criticism over her participation in women’s cricket in Australia, saying she has scientific evidence to show that she does not have an unfair physical advantage.Bangar, the daughter of former India cricketer and ex-batting coach Sanjay Bangar, played age-group men’s cricket for Mumbai before beginning her gender transition in 2022. She underwent gender-affirming surgery in March 2026.The 25-year-old has been cleared by Cricket Australia to play women’s cricket at community level in Australia, subject to its policy requirements.Bangar told the UK-based Daily Mail that she wanted to use the criticism surrounding her eligibility to create more awareness about transgender athletes and the process they go through."I'm willing to take that and basically try to turn that into education and awareness, which I intend to do through my case and many other people out there who have gone through the same process as me and don't have any unfair advantage," she said, as quoted by Daily Mail."I think that's where it all comes down to, and I hope people eventually understand."As part of research at the Manchester University Institute of Sport, Bangar was assessed after more than a year of hormone replacement therapy and testosterone suppression, Daily Mail report said. Researchers looked at her lung capacity, power output and haemoglobin levels and compared the results with those of cisgender female athletes.Bangar said the measurements from the research fell within the range recorded among cisgender female athletes."Whatever data that suggested, it all fell within that range," Bangar said.She said her argument was based on the results of the research rather than her personal views."I'm not talking from personal feelings or opinions. I have actual scientific evidence backing my case. My advocacy in this part is that not all trans women have an unfair advantage. It needs to be assessed on a case-by-case basis, similar to how Cricket Australia has approached my case, and I think that's how it should be worldwide as well."Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: Bills vs. Texans bold predictions for Week 1 of 2026 NFL season
articles.summary: The Buffalo Bills are at a crossroads. This is a team that has been to the playoffs for seven consecutive seasons, and they have fallen short of reaching th...
articles.body:
The Buffalo Bills are at a crossroads. This is a team that has been to the playoffs for seven consecutive seasons, and they have fallen short of reaching the Super Bowl in each of them. Quarterback Josh Allen has been at the helm of their offense in each of those years, and while he is clearly a gifted athlete who plays with courage, skill and intelligence, every one of those season have ended in disappointment.

The Bills have made a dramatic change heading into the 2026 season. They have parted company with their head coach Sean McDermott, a man who had inspired the team and had earned much of the credit for the team's growth. Unfortunately, there were aspects to his leadership that led to some of the postseason failures and the Bills made the powerful and emotional move, and they hired Joe Brady to serve as the new head coach.

Brady had been the architect of Buffalo's explosive offense, and now he is in charge of the full operation. He brought in Jim Leonhard to straighten out the defense and veteran Pete Carmichael will serve as his offensive coordinator.

Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial)

The coaching brain trust knows it has a quarterback in Allen who is ready to lead the team to a championship. He is 30 years old and still at the peak of his abilities. He has the arm strength, leadership, athletic ability and experience to get the job done.

It begins in Week 1 with a demanding road game against the Houston Texans . It is not a must game, as others will be described later in the season, but it is about setting a tone for the season.

Allen will be prepared to make an opening statement

Allen and the Bills will be competing against a formidable pass rush led by Danielle Hunter and Will Anderson . The Bills will be ready to make a statement, and Allen will lead the way.

He has a crew of wide receivers that is led by former Bear D.J. Moore and Khalil Shakir . Both have athletic ability, high-level skill and a desire to make the plays needed to win games. Moore helped take the Bears offense from the bottom of the league to respectability and then to great heights last year. He will give the Bills great leadership when the game is on the line.

Running back James Cook has explosive speed and is coming off a spectacular season in which he rushed for 1,621 yards, 12 touchdowns and a 5.2 yards per carry average.

The production of Moore and Cook will help Allen open the season with a bang. Look for the four-time Pro Bowler and 2024 MVP to throw for 325 yards, 2 touchdowns and run for another score.

Stroud will attempt to climb the QB ladder

Just as Allen faces the pressure of having to lead the Bills to a Super Bowl, Stroud is under a similar pressure to take the Texans deep into the playoffs.

There were rumors at the end of the season that the Texans would be looking to move Stroud after a poor performance in the playoff loss to the New England Patriots , but general manager Nick Caserio said those ideas were "moronic."

He was brilliant in 2023, his rookie season, but he has not been at that level since. Stroud completed 273 of 423 passes for 3,041 yards with 19 touchdowns and 8 interceptions last year. Those numbers don't compare to his rookie season in which he threw for 4,108 yards with a 23 to 5 TD to interception ratio.

Stroud does not have the skilled receivers that Allen has, but Nico Collins and former Patriot Kayshon Boutte are more than competent.

Former Lion David Montgomery will be the key to an improved running attack. The Texans acquired him in an offseason trade and immediately gave him a 2-year, $16.5 million contract extension. Montgomery has exceeded the 1,000-yard mark twice in his career, and he should be able to come close to that level with the Texans.

He needs to set the tone for Stroud and the offense with 80 rushing yards against the Bills. If he can do that, look for Stroud to throw for 250 yards and 2 touchdowns in the season opener.

Bills to outlast Texans with late defensive stand

The Bills and the Texans will be two of the strongest teams in the AFC, and they should be able to play one of the most notable games of the NFL's opening weekend.

However, since teams rarely play their starters in the preseason, the early games in the regular season are often rife with mistakes. The Bills will make their share and so will the Texans, but there is perhaps a bit more for the Bills to fight for because they have been so close to NFL glory so many times.

The Bills are switching to a 3-4 defense this year and that should fit right in with Greg Rousseau , who moves from edge rusher to stand-up outside linebacker. He led the team with 7.0 sacks last season, and he will make the key plays at the end of the game for n improved Buffalo defense.

The Bills will win the game by a 28-24 score.

articles.title: Carlos Alcaraz sends message to Ben Shelton on social media after losing to him at the US Open
articles.summary: Carlos Alcaraz was magnanimous in defeat earlier this week, after losing arguably the match of the tournament to Ben Shelton. It saw his hugely impressive...
articles.body:
Carlos Alcaraz was magnanimous in defeat earlier this week, after losing arguably the match of the tournament to Ben Shelton.

It saw his hugely impressive US Open run come to an end, decided in the most dramatic fashion by a fifth-set tiebreaker.

Before the event began, few expected the Spaniard to even get past the first week given how long he had been out for. To have reached the quarter-finals, and been so close to the semi-finals, must represent a great success.

He is clearly of that mind, and now, not long after Alcaraz issued a fitness update following that match, he has taken to Instagram to send his congratulations to Ben Shelton .

Carlos Alcaraz's parting message for Ben Shelton after losing at the US Open

Carlos Alcaraz 's first claim was one few could dispute: "What a battle Ben!"

It was a battle, lasting just shy of four and a half hours and finishing beyond 3:30 am, the latest in US Open history.

He continued: "You deserve the win, I wish you the best for the rest of the tournament! I leave here happy with my level after such a long injury. Thank you for the energy NYC! Always a very special place!"

Shelton simply replied: "Legend". He also made his own post, which read: "BELIEVE! @carlitosalcarazz what a match… ur an animal and sports icon. tennis needs you."

Alcaraz also spoke positively about Shelton's serve , and how he felt it proved pivotal in winning him their match.

Carlos Alcaraz's behind-the-scenes reaction to his loss to Ben Shelton says everything

Whilst privacy has been taken more seriously ever since Gauff started a movement at the Australian Open , there are still some behind-the-scenes shots which provide fans with a raw, more authentic reaction to such crushing losses.

Just days ago, Alex Eala was pictured looking emotional, rubbing her eyes after losing her iconic US Open battle to Iva Jovic.

However, the video that has emerged of Alcaraz's walk through the tunnel out of Arthur Ashe Stadium showed quite contrasting emotions.

Instead of looking downbeat, his head was held high, and he smiled, even laughed, he strode back to the locker room.

He knows this is just the beginning of his comeback, and this image of him smiling after such a heartbreaking defeat could prove to be quite iconic when we see him back winning the sport's biggest honours again. Given his performance over the last week and a half, we shouldn't have to wait long.

articles.title: ‘A big blow to the Dodgers’: Shohei Ohtani injury sparks concern
articles.summary: Los Angeles Dodgers superstar Shohei Ohtani has missed six of the team’s last seven games due to discomfort in his right arm. Now, the Dodgers have decided t...
articles.body:
Los Angeles Dodgers superstar Shohei Ohtani has missed six of the team's last seven games due to discomfort in his right arm. Now, the Dodgers have decided to place him on the injured list.

After the Dodgers' 14-1 victory over the Cincinnati Reds on Wednesday night, manager Dave Roberts told reporters that Ohtani would be placed on the injured list. The team will also call up top outfield prospect Josue De Paula from Double-A to temporarily fill in for Ohtani at designated hitter.

Ohtani has not pitched since July 3 because of soreness in his left knee, which resurfaced when he attempted to throw his latest bullpen session on Aug. 28. On Monday, Ohtani admitted that he will "most likely" not pitch again this season. However, the two-way superstar has also been dealing with health issues on the offensive side.

The latest injury concerns emerged last Wednesday, when Ohtani shook his right arm while heading into the dugout following a 10th-inning strikeout. He was subsequently left out of the lineup the next day before also missing Friday, Saturday, and Sunday.

Ohtani returned Monday and went 0-for-3 with a walk and two strikeouts, but he was back out of the lineup Tuesday. Roberts revealed that Ohtani experienced pain in his right arm during one of his swings Monday, leading the Dodgers to take the possibility of an injured-list stint more seriously.

Following Wednesday's game, Roberts officially confirmed the decision.

Roberts told reporters that placing Ohtani on the IL was "the right thing to do," while adding, "We tried to kick the can as much as we could."

Despite the decision, Roberts said he was "very" confident that Ohtani would be healthy enough to rejoin the Dodgers when the postseason gets underway.

"If it were a postseason game tomorrow, he would be in the lineup," Roberts said via ESPN . "Now you're talking about two weeks, 14 days. I feel that it's that substantial. He'll be in a much better place than he was today. Is it gonna be 100%? Probably not. But I do think, with this time that we're taking now, he'll be in an adequate spot to finish the season and beyond."

Needless to say, this news led to a lot of reactions and concern on social media.

"Look, only the Dodgers and Ohtani truly know how serious this is. But after everything we learned today, I think it's safe to say we're headed toward an IL stint — and honestly, I wouldn't expect to see Ohtani again until October. Why risk making it worse? The NL West is essentially wrapped up, and the Dodgers have a three-game cushion over Atlanta for the No. 2 seed. Get healthy. Stay healthy. Get ready for October," wrote Cody Snavely of DodgersBeat.

"It's a big blow to the Dodgers, and Dave Roberts claiming Shohei Ohtani might not return at 100 percent for the postseason is a bit more concerning," wrote sportswriter Victor Okechukwu .

"I do think that the Dodgers are going to 'turn it on' in October and make a run at least to the NLCS, BUT baseball is a long unforgiving year. There's a reason 3-peats have only happened 4 times before. (Again, not that Dodgers can't, they can, but it's not a foregone conclusion)," added another fan .

"It's almost as if humans weren't meant to pitch and hit. Who knew?" another fan wrote .

Ohtani's earliest possible return from the 15-day IL will come on Sept. 23. We'll have to see when the Dodgers welcome him back.

articles.title: Joe Brady triples number of Bills captains in first season as coach
articles.summary: Josh Allen and Terrel Bernard return as Bills captains, but four players join them as Buffalo expands its leadership group under Joe Brady.
articles.body:
The Buffalo Bills have more captains this season. Three times more.

Buffalo named six captains for the 2026 season, tripling the number from each of the previous two years as Joe Brady begins his first season as head coach.

Quarterback Josh Allen and linebacker Terrel Bernard remain captains, but they're joined by tight end Dawson Knox , outside linebacker Bradley Chubb , long snapper Reid Ferguson and defensive back Sam Franklin Jr.

The group is evenly divided with two captains apiece on offense, defense and special teams.

Allen is a captain for the eighth consecutive season. Bernard earned the designation for the third straight year.

Knox and Chubb are the new captains on offense and defense. It's the first captain designation for Knox, who is entering his seventh NFL season, while Chubb was a captain with the Miami Dolphins last season before signing with Buffalo as a free agent in the offseason.

Ferguson, the longest-tenured player on the Bills roster and entering his 11th season with the Bills, is a captain for the third time. Franklin rounds out the group as a special teams captain.

The six captains represents a significant change from the past two seasons.

Allen and Bernard were Buffalo's only designated captains in 2024 and 2025. Allen has been a captain every season since 2019, his second year in the league. The Bills also used a 10-player leadership council in 2024.

The Bills had eight captains in 2023 and nine in 2022, the most during Sean McDermott's nine seasons as head coach.

Brady has returned to a larger group in his first season running the team.

The new leadership group will make its debut Sunday when the Bills open the regular season against the Houston Texans at Reliant Stadium.

QB Josh Allen: Eighth consecutive season

LB Terrel Bernard: Third consecutive season

OLB Bradley Chubb: First season with Buffalo; captain with Miami in 2025

articles.title: ‘Horrible Game From Drake (Maye), Disgusting’ — Barstool Sports’ Dave Portnoy Rips Patriots QB After Meek Week 1 Loss to Seahawks
articles.summary: The New England Patriots opened the season with a result that has quickly turned optimism into frustration. A promising 10-0 start against the Seattle Seahaw...
articles.body:
The New England Patriots opened the season with a result that has quickly turned optimism into frustration. A promising 10-0 start against the Seattle Seahawks on Wednesday night disappeared as the Patriots struggled to finish drives and protect their lead against a team that lost its quarterback on the opening drive.

The defeat also placed quarterback Drake Maye at the center of postgame criticism, with one of the Patriots' most outspoken supporters making his feelings clear.

Dave Portnoy Gives Drake Maye, Patriots "F-Minus" After Loss to Seahawks

Barstool Sports founder and longtime Patriots fan Dave Portnoy did not hold back after New England fell 13-10 to Seattle at Lumen Field.

Portnoy singled out Maye's abysmal passing and interceptions in the final quarter while also criticizing the offense, the team's receiving production, and the way the Patriots handled a game they had under control early.

"Only the first game, only the first game of the season, but that was tough to watch," Portnoy said . "Horrible game from Drake, that last throw. Disgusting. We lose A.J. Brown with what I guess is going to be a pretty severe injury.

"The other guy, the new guy, [Romeo] Doubs, just does a disgusting drop. Play calling sucked most of the night, I thought, on offense. The game was right there for the taking. Obviously, it's only Week 1, but that was a [expletive] way to start the season. Could be a lot better than that. That was F-minus [expletive]."

Maye's three interceptions made his night particularly difficult. His final turnover came with less than 30 seconds remaining, when he threw into the end zone instead of helping the Patriots position themselves for a potential game-tying field goal. Seattle's Josh Jobe came down with the interception, ending New England's final opportunity.

BE THE GM OF YOUR FAVORITE TEAM: PFN's Free NFL Mock Draft Simulator

The earlier turnovers also carried consequences.

Maye's first interception followed a tipped pass intended for newcomer Romeo Doubs , while his second came on a third-and-14 throw over the middle that was picked off by Julian Love . Seattle turned both drives into points, helping erase New England's lead of more than one score.

The Patriots also lost A.J. Brown to a right ankle injury in the third quarter, further reducing their offensive options. Doubs, meanwhile, finished without a catch on three targets and dropped a pass before Maye's second interception.

Seattle's comeback came despite starting quarterback Sam Darnold leaving with a hip injury on the opening drive. Drew Lock stepped in and helped the Seahawks rally, while Jaxon Smith-Njigba finished with 122 receiving yards and a touchdown.

Coach Mike Vrabel acknowledged the disappointment but urged the Patriots to learn from their mistakes and move forward with the long season ahead.

"I'm disappointed, but, like I said, we'll never accept losing, but we have to embrace being able to move on and improve, and we know how long the season is," Vrabel said .

articles.title: Commanders' first injury report of 2026: Good news ahead of Week 1
articles.summary: The Commanders' first injury report for the 2026 season is mostly positive.
articles.body:
Just two weeks ago, Commanders Nation was ablaze with fear and anxiety.

Nick Allegretti had returned only for one day before being injured again. Bill Croskey-Merritt pulled up late in practice and missed the next week of practices. K'Lavon Chaisson couldn't practice, Marcus Mariota missed the last two preseason games with an injured knee, and Jordan Magee injured a shoulder in the preseason and was kept out of practices. Odafe Oweh (calf) was out, and Ben Sinnott had just pulled an oblique, and he was unable to practice.

Two weeks later, Wednesday was the first official injury report for the Commanders. The news was mostly good. Things are definitely trending up for the team's health. Oweh, Croskey-Merritt, and Chaisson are each now back in practice. One caveat: all three were listed as "limited".

Allegretti, Magee, Mariota, Charles Omenihu, and Sinnott are listed as full participants for Wednesday. That's great news. So the world isn't going to burn up in twelve years, as we were led to believe a couple of weeks ago.

The panic from the fan base and local media that quickly settled over the area was perhaps most due to the 2025 season itself. When injuries began to pile up in training camp, we all thought of 2025: missed games by starters, the plummeting of the team's health, and the resulting slide to 5-12.

Head Coach Dan Quinn, on Wednesday, didn't want to talk much about injuries. He said everyone was practicing, but cautioned that not everyone was practicing at the same level, which would mean the same intensity or practice duration.

The Commanders will travel to face the Philadelphia Eagles on Sunday, September 13. Kickoff is set for 4:25 PM, and FOX will televise the game.

articles.title: Poor miscues cost LA Galaxy in shutout road loss to Vancouver
articles.summary: After a conceded goal put the LA Galaxy down at the eighth minute, the team struggled to bounce back in a measly 3-0 loss to the Vancouver Whitecaps on the r...
articles.body:
After a conceded goal put the LA Galaxy down at the eighth minute, the team struggled to bounce back in a measly 3-0 loss to the Vancouver Whitecaps on the road on Wednesday night.

The loss marked the fourth time the Galaxy have been shutout since the second half of the season began, a notable development considering they had scored a goal in each match prior to the World Cup break.

Since that break concluded, it has been evident that the Galaxy have struggled to find any sort of rhythm or momentum, despite having many opportunities to do so. After coming out victorious in their latest contest, that chance to build on it was squandered once again.

Vancouver found their rhythm right out of the gates before the Galaxy could create anything interesting on the offensive front.

After a few early chances in the match's opening minutes, Brian White put the Whitecaps ahead with a crafty move right past Galaxy defender Jakob Glesnes in the box and finding the back of the net. Julian Aude had lost the ball on a poor effort just moments beforehand, creating a chance for Vancouver in poor territory.

From that point on, the pressure did not slow down from the Vancouver offense in the first half. Despite being held to a 1-0 lead heading into halftime, JT Marcinkowski did all he could to keep the Galaxy competitive in the game.

The Galaxy made necessary adjustments to keep their spirit alive – which was led by Marcinkowski defensively and Kyōgo Furuhashi pushing the offense well enough to pressure the Whitecaps.

However, shortly into the start of the second half came another miscue that would prove costly in the momentum category.

In the 57th minute, a pass to Galaxy midfielder Erik Thommy was botched as he slipped before he could handle the ball, which created a chance for Ryan Gauld to navigate his way through the defense and slip a ball into the left corner of the net.

It was the Galaxy's second conceded goal by way of mishandling the ball, this time around on a poor giveaway. However, it wasn't exactly the stamp on the poor night for the Galaxy.

Vancouver would go on to cap off the night with a third goal at the 90th minute on a penalty, which came on a poor tackling effort from Emiro Garces. Bruno Caicedo converted on a ball that was tipped by Marcinkowski to put an end to the Galaxy's disappointing night.

The Galaxy, who sit just one point away from a playoff spot along with two other clubs, will hope for a better fortune on Saturday night when they host the Seattle Sounders , who narrowly trail the Galaxy in the Western Conference standings.

articles.title: Jaxon Smith-Njigba picks up where he left off
articles.summary: Despite the early switch from Sam Darnold (hip) to Drew Lock, Jaxon Smith-Njigba still topped 100 yards and scored Seattle's lone touchdown.
articles.body:
Seattle Seahawks WR Jaxon Smith-Njigba totaled eight receptions, 122 yards, and a touchdown during the team's Week 1 win over the New England Patriots . He was targeted a game-high 11 times.

Why It Matters: Give some credit to Drew Lock , who found ways to get the ball to JSN after Sam Darnold (hip) was knocked out of the game after just one drive due to a hip injury. That Lock was able to step in and help Smith-Njigba top 100 yards is great news for JSN owners -- one need only look at Justin Jefferson a season ago to see how a quarterback can kill a talented receiver's fantasy value. No matter who starts at quarterback in Week 2, Smith-Njigba should remain locked in fantasy lineups as a WR1.

articles.title: Ciriaco - The Pyjamas
articles.summary: Sometimes, the meme takes on a life of its own. Even before social media existed. There is a reason why the footballing legacy of a Swiss midfielder has been...
articles.body:
Sometimes, the meme takes on a life of its own. Even before social media existed. There is a reason why the footballing legacy of a Swiss midfielder has been overshadowed by a single scene from a film.

Massimo Moratti wanted to completely transform the way his Inter side played. When he took over the Club in early 1995, Ottavio Bianchi was already at the helm. He had previously guided Napoli to the Scudetto with Diego Maradona in his side. There was no Maradona in that Inter side, however: instead, their attacking options included Branca, Ganz and Benny Carbone.

Bianchi soon departed and was replaced by the Switzerland head coach, whose national team played attractive, attacking football in a zonal system, as virtually everyone did by then. The man in question was Englishman Roy Hodgson, and one of his masterstrokes had been turning an attack-minded midfielder into a holding player. Ciriaco Sforza, stationed in front of the defence, was the secret behind that Switzerland side.

After securing European qualification in the final seconds of the final game through a Delvecchio goal, Hodgson made Sforza his main transfer request the following summer. At the time, the midfielder was playing for Bayern Munich . His first Serie A appearance brought his first goal: a stunning long-range strike in Udine that secured victory on the opening day. Udinese 0-1 Inter, with Sforza the match-winner. It looked like the beginning of a perfect marriage, but it would remain the only real high point. Well, almost.

His tactical partnership with Paul Ince, the star of the team, proved difficult. Despite playing regularly, Sforza never truly shone. He was eventually sold to Kaiserslautern on 22 July, by which time the new season was already underway and personalised shirts were available in sports shops.

That same July, three Italian comedians and lifelong Inter fans were shooting a film almost for fun. Tre uomini e una gamba would go on to become one of the biggest commercial successes in the history of Italian cinema. It also featured a scene that would become immortal. Giacomo had to spend a night in hospital but did not have any pyjamas, so he borrowed a pair from his friend Aldo. The rest is history:

Nearly 30 years after the film hit cinemas, Sforza - a surname steeped in Milanese nobility - still holds a unique place in Italian football pop culture. And it has little to do with what Ciriaco produced on the pitch.

articles.title: Virgil van Dijk's successor has been found by Liverpool, it's not Jeremy Jacquet
articles.summary: One of the hardest players for Liverpool to replace in the future will be Virgil van Dijk. The 35-year-old is entering the final year of his contract with th...
articles.body:
One of the hardest players for Liverpool to replace in the future will be Virgil van Dijk .

The 35-year-old is entering the final year of his contract with the Anfield outfit and, at the moment, no talks about a new deal have been shared.

Obviously, since he's likely to start most of Liverpool's games again this season, the Reds will probably enter negotiations with their captain at some point.

In fact, he's even said himself that, since he didn't hit his peak until late on in his career that he could continue playing at the top level for a lot longer than people think.

However, with him now getting to the twilight stages of his career, some succession plans are going to have to be put in place for when Van Dijk 's departure actually occurs.

So, the fact that the Reds are already being linked with top-level centre-backs is massively reassuring.

Liverpool now keeping a 'close eye' on Malick Thiaw

This summer, Liverpool's defence had a fair few new players added to it.

Jeremy Jacquet and Ronald Araujo were the two players added to Liverpool's ranks in the transfer window but, with Giovanni Leoni also returning from injury, the Italian is basically a new signing.

Each of these players will have a major part to play for the Reds this term but, it's unclear whether they'd be able to live up to the standards that Van Dijk has set.

The towering Dutchman has easily been one of the Premier League's best centre-backs over the last few years and, a Liverpool team without him among their starting XI feels weird to even think about.

However, as mentioned, since he's getting on a bit now, some changes may have to be made so, the fact that Caught Offside have linked the Reds with a move for Malick Thiaw in the future makes a lot of sense.

"Liverpool and Manchester United are both keeping a close eye on Newcastle United defender Malick Thiaw as they assess potential defensive reinforcements for future transfer windows," they wrote .

"Sources close to the agents industry have informed CaughtOffside that Liverpool and Man United have been monitoring Thiaw's performances, although no formal negotiations or direct talks have taken place.

"Liverpool's interest is particularly understandable given the questions surrounding their defence.

" Virgil van Dijk is approaching the latter stages of his Anfield career, while Andoni Iraola will eventually need another centre-back capable of becoming a long-term starter.

"Liverpool have actually monitored Thiaw before.

"Thiaw is contracted until 2029 and would reportedly command around £65m-£70m, despite a market valuation closer to €45m."

Malick Thiaw would be a perfect signing for Liverpool

Before Thiaw joined Newcastle a couple of summers ago, he was a relatively unknown entity in England.

But, abroad, he was sought-after. Now, the centre-back is 25 years old and started his career with Schalke.

From then, in in the 2022-23 season, he joined AC Milan where he was a regular feature.

He then joined Newcastle and, within the two years he's been at St James' Park, he's quickly become one of their most important players.

That is, especially now that Anthony Gordon , Bruno Guimaraes and Sandro Tonali have all left.

During his time as a Newcastle players, he's earned plenty of Premier League experience and has even featured in 11 Champions League games.

Of course, nobody will ever be able to replace Van Dijk but, a 25-year-old centre-back with a decent chunk of top flight experience could definitely eventually become as good as the Dutchman.

Obviously, a deal would cost Liverpool a lot to get over the line but, if they're serious about competing for silverware every year, they're going to have to start making these costly moves to try and get an advantage over their rivals.

articles.title: 'If Mac Allister's performances are good, he will get a new contract'
articles.summary: Former Liverpool defender Stephen Warnock said Alexis Mac Allister just needed to be put into a system that suits him to get the best out of him.  "I don't t...
articles.body:
Former Liverpool defender Stephen Warnock said Alexis Mac Allister just needed to be put into a system that suits him to get the best out of him.

"I don't think he has to show his importance to Liverpool, I think everyone knows the qualities he has got anyway," said Warnock, who was a pundit on Wednesday's Champions League Match of the Day.

"There will be a lot of talk about him because of what has gone on in the past few days, but Liverpool fans were already asking why hasn't he been offered a new contract when other players have.

"To come out and talk about a contract situation like he did, a couple of days before a game, and to be able to back it up the way he did with a good performance is important - but it is over the course of the season where his performances are important. If he wants a contract and he thinks he deserves a contract, then if his performances are good, he will get one.

"We all know the qualities that he has got - he is a World Cup winner, a Premier League winner - it is just that he has got to be put into the right system to make it work.

"At the moment, Liverpool's system is a little bit dysfunctional, but it is starting to get better and he will get better because of that."

articles.title: Champions Seahawks beat Patriots in season opener
articles.summary: Defending champions the Seattle Seahawks come from behind to beat the New England Patriots 13-10 in the opening game of the NFL season.
articles.body:
Defending champions the Seattle Seahawks came from behind to beat the New England Patriots 13-10 in the opening game of the NFL season.

For the first time in 10 years the season began with a rematch of the Super Bowl, in which the Patriots were dominated by a Seahawks defence known as 'the Dark Side'.

Again they stepped up after Seattle lost quarterback Sam Darnold to a hip injury in the game's opening drive, claiming three interceptions in the final quarter at Lumen Field.

The Patriots went into a 10-0 lead, with rookie tight end Eli Raridon scoring the first touchdown of the season in the second quarter.

Back-up quarterback Drew Lock got the Seattle offence going late in the third quarter, with Jason Myers cutting the gap with a field goal.

Seahawks cornerback Nehemiah Pritchett claimed his first career interception at the start of the fourth quarter, after a Drake Maye pass was deflected by rookie Rodney Thomas.

On the next possession Lock found wide reciever Jaxon Smith-Njigba in space and last season's offensive player of the year charged through the Patriots defence for a 45-yard touchdown.

Julian Love then picked off Patriots quarterback Maye, giving Myers the chance to edge the Seahawks in front with a 26-yard field goal.

New England were well within field-goal range with 21 seconds remaining, but chose to go for the win rather than settle for overtime, and the move backfired as Maye's hopeful pass towards Mack Hollins was intercepted by Josh Jobe in the end zone.

The only game in which Maye threw multiple interceptions last season was the Super Bowl, and he was picked off on the Patriots' final three possessions in the season opener.

Seattle head coach Mike Macdonald said initial tests showed Darnold had not fractured a hip.

Week one continues with the NFL's first regular-season game in Australia. The Los Angeles Rams meet the San Francisco 49ers in Melbourne on Thursday (01:35 BST, Friday).
